record.title: Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council: Report adopted pursuant to Article 112(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on the need to review the list of prohibited AI practices and of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
record.summary: The Commission's first report under Article 112(1) of the AI Act on whether the list of prohibited AI practices in Article 5 and the high-risk use cases in Annex III need to be amended. Drawing on consultation of Member States through the AI Board, a multi-stakeholder consultation and an analysis of AI incident databases, it identifies a potential regulatory gap for AI systems generating child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate content, which Article 5 does not prohibit. It flags other systems for monitoring, among them emotion recognition, AI companions and mental-health chatbots, and political disinformation.
record.notes: Adopted on 20 May 2026 and addressed to the European Parliament and the Council. It does not review the list of areas in Annex III, which Article 112(2) requires by 2 August 2028. The report finds its assessment limited: when it was adopted, the rules on enforcing the prohibitions applied only from 2 August 2026, national competent authorities were still being designated and the Commission's guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems were still in preparation. It refers to the Commission's proposal for a Digital Omnibus on AI, which would tie the start of the high-risk rules to the availability of standards and support tools, no later than 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems. The next assessment under Article 112 is due in 2026. A summary of the report by Portugal's Agency for Technological Reform of the State says that the political agreement of 7 May 2026 between the Commission and the European Parliament on the AI Omnibus introduced a specific prohibition of AI systems generating non-consensual intimate content or child sexual abuse material into the AI Act.

verification.note: Re-read in the recheck of 17 Oct 2026: the EUR-Lex HTML of COM(2026) 234 final (official, stored 11 Oct 2026) is the report's own full text; it confirms the title, the date (Brussels, 20.5.2026), the Article 112(1) basis, the methodology and the findings. The same EUR-Lex file is also stored as a source of EU-14 and EU-06. Stored in this run: a news item of 5 June 2026 by ARTE, the Portuguese Agency for Technological Reform of the State (digital.gov.pt), which summarises the report and reports the 7 May 2026 AI Omnibus agreement adding a prohibition of systems generating non-consensual intimate content or CSAM. That item says the report refers to the agreement, but the stored EUR-Lex text mentions the Digital Omnibus only as a proposal still under negotiation. Version 1's summary said the report concludes there is no immediate need to amend Article 5 or Annex III; the report uses that wording only for emotion recognition, and the summary now follows its conclusions. Version 1's date of 2 Dec 2026 for the new prohibition is not in this record's stored files and was removed.

title.quote: REPORT FROM THE COMMISSION TO THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL REPORT ADOPTED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 112(1) OF REGULATION (EU) 2024/1689 ON THE NEED TO REVIEW THE LIST OF PROHIBITED AI PRACTICES AND OF HIGH-RISK AI SYSTEMS LISTED IN ANNEX III

status.quote: This report is prepared by the Commission and addressed to the European Parliament and the Council to fulfil the Commission’s obligations as set out in the Article 112(1) AI Act.
This is the first report adopted under that provision.
The European Commission has published the annual report required by Article 112(1) of the AI Act.

legal_force.quote: The findings set out in this report are submitted for the consideration of these institutions.

summary.quote: Its objective is to assess whether there is a need to amend the list of use cases set out in Annex III and the list of prohibited AI practices laid down in Article 5 AI Act
Engagement with the AI Board and consultation with Member States and national competent authorities
A multi-stakeholder consultation was conducted to collect feedback and perspectives from a broad range of stakeholders
Empirical research: analysing AI incident databases
the Commission notes and further analyse a potential regulatory gap regarding AI systems generating CSAM and non-consensual intimate content, which are not prohibited by Article 5 AI Act
However, this area is flagged for further consideration.
in light of the increasing proliferation of AI companions and AI mental support chatbots, the Commission considers it important to closely monitor their development
The analysis led to the identification of the following areas flagged for further monitoring and data collection: A significant number of incidents involved political disinformation campaigns

notes.quote: The review of the list of areas covered by Annex III falls outside the scope of this report, as the Commission is only required to conduct that review by 2 August 2028, in accordance with Article 112(2) AI Act.
the rules on the enforcement of that chapter will only apply as from 2 August 2026 and the national competent authorities are still in the process of being designated
guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems are still under preparation
The Commission proposed in the Digital Omnibus on AI to align the timeline for the high-risk AI rules to the availability of standards and other support tools.
the rules will start to apply after a 6-month transition period for high-risk AI systems in Annex III and in any case no later than 2 December 2027
The next assessment of the Commission pursuant to Article 112 AI Act is therefore due in 2026

the political agreement reached on 7 May 2026 between the Commission and the European Parliament as part of the simplified 'AI Omnibus' legislative package, which introduced a specific prohibition on these systems into the text of the Regulation
The report identifies a potential regulatory gap concerning AI systems that generate non-consensual intimate content or child sexual abuse material.

changes.title: the report's own title from its cover page: version 1 left out 'Report adopted pursuant to Article 112(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689'
changes.summary: rewritten to follow the report's conclusions: it notes a potential gap for CSAM and non-consensual intimate content and flags other systems for monitoring; 'no immediate need to amend' is the report's wording for emotion recognition only; the methodology added
changes.notes: rewritten from the report; the Digital Omnibus prohibition date (2 Dec 2026) removed; the report's own account of the Omnibus proposal added, and the 7 May 2026 agreement adding the prohibition from the Portuguese government agency's summary
changes.related: EU-14 added: the report refers to the forthcoming high-risk classification guidelines

judgment.status_reasoning: A Commission report adopted on 20 May 2026 and submitted to the European Parliament and the Council; a report does not lapse, and no corrigendum or replacement is shown. The next annual report under Article 112(1) would be a separate instrument. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A Commission report required by the AI Act on prohibited practices and high-risk use cases; in scope with no note.

extra_urls.reason: news item of 5 June 2026 by ARTE, the Portuguese Agency for Technological Reform of the State (digitalGOV portal), on this report: it reports that the political agreement of 7 May 2026 on the AI Omnibus introduced a specific prohibition of AI systems generating non-consensual intimate content or CSAM, the gap the report identified; another official source for the follow-up in notes

open_questions: The Portuguese agency's summary says the report refers to the 7 May 2026 AI Omnibus agreement, but the stored EUR-Lex text (generated 20 May 2026) mentions the Omnibus only as a proposal under negotiation; is there a later version of the report's text?

The same summary gives a Commission page for the report, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/report-review-prohibitions-and-high-risk-ai, which is not stored; a later run could store it as secondary_url.
Version 1's notes said the new Article 5 prohibition from the Digital Omnibus applies from 2 Dec 2026; that date is in EU-18's sources, not in this record's stored files.
